articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA contractor just casually left AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like it's some kind of amateur hour speedrun of federal incompetence. Because nothing says "cybersecurity leadership" like publicly exposing your crown jewels to every script kiddie with a browser.

articles.title: 'Claw Chain' Vulnerabilities Threaten OpenClaw Deployments
articles.summary: Microsoft Exchange getting pwned by an XSS zero-day with no patch in sight. Classic Microsoft move: ship first, security later, patch never.

articles.title: The New Phishing Click: How OAuth Consent Bypasses MFA
articles.summary: NGINX Rift vulnerability gets weaponized faster than you can say "responsible disclosure" — because nothing motivates attackers quite like an 18-year-old flaw finally seeing daylight. The internet's favorite web server just became everyone's favorite target.

articles.title: Looking Back, Looking Forward: Digesting a Dynamic Bouillabaisse of Cyber Evolution
articles.summary: Instagram quietly murdered its end-to-end encryption feature, proving once again that Meta's privacy promises have the lifespan of a mayfly. Years of public commitments just got Zucked into the digital graveyard.

articles.title: Anthropic Will Update Regulators on Mythos’ Cyber Vulnerability Findings
articles.summary: GitHub Actions workflow gets hijacked to steal CI/CD credentials because apparently even our automation tools need trust issues now. Every tag redirected to malicious commits — it's like a supply chain attack with commitment issues.

articles.title: We Updated Our Privacy Policy. Here's What Changed and Why.
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud, proving that even elite social engineers eventually get caught by the oldest trick in the book: consequences. Another legend falls to the feds' patient game.

articles.title: Millions Impacted Across Several US Healthcare Data Breaches
articles.summary: Grafana tells ransomware crew to pound sand after GitHub hack, refusing to pay extortion demands like absolute legends. Sometimes the good guys do have spines after all.

articles.title: Your 401(k) is the new identity theft target
articles.summary: ShinyHunters strikes again, this time harvesting 600k+ Salesforce records from 7-Eleven because even convenience stores aren't convenient enough to secure properly. Your Slurpee data is now dark web commodity.

articles.title: Help EFF Solve an Issue That's Bigger than Creepy Ads
articles.summary: EFF drops new guide on fighting surveillance abuses because apparently we need a manual to explain why mass digital stalking is bad. When basic human rights require instruction manuals, democracy has left the building.

articles.title: Linux kernel flaw opens root-only files to unprivileged users
articles.summary: Shai-Hulud worm continues its npm package infection spree like some kind of JavaScript plague rat. Four more packages compromised by the same persistent scumbag — the gift that keeps on giving malware.
